extracted.subtask_description: A practical craft guide for writing, testing, and refining stand-up jokes and long bits, drawn from Patton Oswalt's notes and threads. Focuses on specificity, source material, structure for long bits, avoiding hack premises, and concrete rehearsal/process habits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specificity as Imagination's Disguise
rubrics_metrics.description: Specificity is what makes the audience trust you've actually thought about it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use very concrete, specific details (example: 'A bag of Vienna sausages' is funnier than 'snacks'). Specificity is described as the cheapest, most reliable laugh upgrade — it signals thought and creates stronger associations for jokes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reading Outside Comedy
rubrics_metrics.description: Pros read history, philosophy, and weird genre fiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broaden reading to seed associations ordinary stand-ups don't have; the originality of a joke is often the originality of the referent. Use non-comedy references to create unexpected connections and fresh angles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oswalt 'Inside' Bit / Long Bit Structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Long bits work when they're a constructed argument disguised as a story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure long bits as: small detail → larger frame → unexpected synthesis. The audience stays engaged because the comic is BUILDING something rather than merely naming items; ensure the bit is moving toward that synthesis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hack vs. Hack-Adjacent Premise
rubrics_metrics.description: A hack premise is one whose joke shape is on rails. A hack-adjacent premise is one whose subject is overdone but whose angle is yours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classify premises: hack = dead (too predictable), hack-adjacent = salvageable if you bring a unique angle. Prioritize finding genuinely original angles rather than relying on over-familiar subjects unless you can make the angle unmistakably yours.

rubrics_metrics.name: Always carry a notebook
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capture ideas immediately; small details and specific images often become the core of jokes. Making a habit of note-taking preserves referents and specificity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test jokes in tiny rooms first
rubrics_metrics.description: Try the joke at a tiny room first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use small rooms as testing grounds to see what lands and to iterate quickly. Avoid debuting untested material in bigger rooms where stakes and expectations are higher.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record every set
rubrics_metrics.description: Record every set; listen at 1.5x speed for pacing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document performances to analyze pacing, rhythm, and audience reaction. Listening at 1.5x speed is recommended for efficient review focused on pacing and timing decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Find one comic whose taste you trust; trade material
rubrics_metrics.description: Find one comic whose taste you trust; trade material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have a trusted peer to give feedback and exchange material with; trading helps refine bits, spot weak premises, and calibrate taste. Seek out one comic whose judgment you respect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is the joke as specific as your actual taste?
rubrics_metrics.description: Working-rubric question: Is the joke as specific as your actual taste?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this as a quick checkpoint on drafts/sets — if the joke feels generic compared to what you truly find funny, push for more specificity until it matches your sensibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is the reference one only YOU could have made?
rubrics_metrics.description: Working-rubric question: Is the reference one only YOU could have made?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate originality of referents; unique, personal, or uncommon references strengthen ownership and distinctiveness of a joke.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is the bit BUILDING toward a synthesis?
rubrics_metrics.description: Working-rubric question: Is the bit BUILDING toward a synthesis?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check long bits for progressive construction — each beat should add toward an unexpected but earned synthesis. If the bit feels like a list or disconnected anecdotes, rework to make it an argument disguised as a story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is the premise hack, hack-adjacent, or genuinely your angle?
rubrics_metrics.description: Working-rubric question: Is the premise hack, hack-adjacent, or genuinely your angle?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Categorize the premise to decide whether to rework or keep: hack = discard, hack-adjacent = re-angle to make it yours, genuinely your angle = proceed and develop.

rubrics_metrics.name: Have you recorded and reviewed the set?
rubrics_metrics.description: Working-rubric question: Have you recorded and reviewed the set?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure recording and post-set review are part of regular practice; reviewing helps identify timing problems, dead spots, and opportunities for tightening.

rubrics_metrics.name: Did you trade with a comic you trust?
rubrics_metrics.description: Working-rubric question: Did you trade with a comic you trust?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify you've solicited peer feedback and exchanged material prior to broader exposure; trusted peers can flag hack premises and suggest stronger beats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specificity as the primary laugh upgrade (summary maxim)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specificity is described as 'the cheapest, most reliable laugh upgrade.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When choosing between edits, favor adding concrete, sensory, or uniquely personal detail because it disproportionately increases comedic payoff relative to the effort.
